_note: Upstream source repositories AnyRealm builds from. Every remote here was verified with `git ls-remote` and is re-checked live at runtime by /api/sources/probe, so this file is a seed, not a frozen truth. A source is listed only with the artifact it actually produces.

kinds.rom: Android custom ROM source tree. Produces system/vendor/product images plus a boot image, i.e. an installable ROM zip or a super image.
kinds.mobile_linux: Mobile Linux distribution source or recipes. Produces an arm64 rootfs and a boot artifact.
kinds.desktop_linux: Desktop Linux distribution source or installer/ISO builder. Produces an x86_64 rootfs and kernel for a NUKI/NURFS ISO.
kinds.kernel: Kernel tree only. Produces Image/Image.lz4 or bzImage plus modules.
kinds.desktop_env: Desktop environment or shell. Not a distro: an addon layer merged into a desktop rootfs, e.g. GNOME or Plasma on top of Debian.
kinds.rom_x86: Android custom ROM or reference tree built for x86_64. This is the only thing that can supply the Android half of the desktop ISO, because that half must run on the Vivobook's x86_64 CPU, not on ARM.

sources.name: LineageOS
sources.note: Broadest device support of the custom ROMs. Per-device trees live under android_device_<vendor>_<device>.
sources.build_hint: repo init -u https://github.com/LineageOS/android.git -b lineage-24.0 && repo sync -c -j8

sources.name: Evolution X
sources.note: Manifest repo. Clone it, then repo sync pulls the tree. Default branch moves (currently cnb).
sources.build_hint: repo init -u https://github.com/Evolution-X/manifest -b vic && repo sync -c -j8

sources.name: Project Elixir
sources.note: Manifest repo. Branches are codenamed (Tiramisu, UNO, snow, vany) rather than version-numbered.

sources.name: DerpFest
sources.note: Manifest repo. Version branches such as 15.2.

sources.name: crDroid
sources.note: LineageOS-based with extra UI work. Device trees mirror LineageOS naming.

sources.name: PixelOS
sources.note: Pixel-flavoured AOSP. Device trees are PixelOS-Devices/*.

sources.name: AOSP (upstream)
sources.note: The reference tree the ROMs fork. No vendor HALs, so it targets emulators and reference boards.

sources.name: Sailfish OS
sources.note: Mer-core kickstart configs, the buildable entry point. The Mer core itself is mirrored per-package under github.com/sailfishos/*; git.sailfishos.org redirects and cannot be cloned anonymously.

sources.name: Mobian
sources.note: Debian-based mobile. Recipes are debos YAML, so they produce an arm64 rootfs image directly.

sources.name: KDE neon
sources.note: Ubuntu core plus rolling KDE packages. The recipes repo (neon/neon-recipes) requires auth, but ubuntu-core is the buildable base and plasma-mobile is in the addons below.
sources.build_hint: git clone https://invent.kde.org/neon/ubuntu-core.git && see its docker-images recipes

sources.name: Ubuntu Touch (UBports)
sources.note: Lomiri user space on an Android-derived HAL. Whole-system rebuild, not a rootfs drop-in.
sources.build_hint: ubports-installer for images; source builds go through the UBports CI recipes

sources.name: Kali NetHunter Pro
sources.note: Full Kali image for phones and ARM laptops, not a layered-over-Android install. This is the user space the desktop ISO merges.
sources.build_hint: prebuilt images published by Kali; source builds use the arm-image recipes

sources.name: Kali NetHunter (layered)
sources.note: Kali user space layered over an existing Android install. GitHub mirror: the GitLab path needs auth.
sources.build_hint: clone, then run the device-specific kernel-builder and rootfs scripts

sources.name: postmarketOS
sources.note: Alpine-based. pmaports holds device packages; pmbootstrap builds the rootfs.

sources.name: Droidian
sources.note: Debian user space on an Android vendor/kernel base. Structurally the closest upstream analogue to NUKI/NURFS.
sources.build_hint: see droidian-recipes; needs an Android device tree for the vendor half

sources.name: Ubuntu
sources.note: Installer source. The rootfs itself comes from debootstrap or live-build.

sources.name: Debian
sources.note: Installer source. Rootfs from debootstrap; this repo is the ISO and installer half.

sources.name: Arch Linux (archiso)
sources.note: Profile-driven ISO builder. Produces a bootable x86_64 ISO directly, so it merges well.

sources.name: Fedora
sources.note: Kickstarts drive livemedia-creator and lorax. The bare pagure path serves HTML; the .git remote is the real one.

sources.name: openSUSE (KIWI)
sources.note: KIWI image builder, which both openSUSE and SUSE use to produce ISOs and appliances.

sources.name: Void Linux
sources.note: mklive produces both live ISOs and rootfs tarballs; musl or glibc, selectable.

sources.name: Gentoo
sources.note: Release engineering specs that catalyst turns into stages and ISOs.

sources.name: Linux Mint
sources.note: Installer used by Mint's Debian edition, plus Mint's Cinnamon stack in the addons.
sources.build_hint: build from a Mint/Ubuntu base with live-build

sources.name: Pop!_OS
sources.note: Ubuntu-based with the COSMIC desktop in the addons. Installer is a Rust rewrite of distinst.
sources.build_hint: see the repo's build scripts; needs a Pop/Ubuntu base

sources.name: Alpine Linux
sources.note: musl-based, so its libc must be isolated and never fused -- the fusion engine enforces this.
sources.build_hint: aports is the package tree; rootfs from alpine-make-rootfs or lbu

sources.name: AR-NUKI-genevn
sources.note: This project's mobile kernel, 5.10.240, Moto G Stylus 5G 2023 (sm6450). Self-sufficient: no build.config glue, SUSFS + ZeroMount + KernelSU-Next in tree.
sources.build_hint: make O=out ARCH=arm64 ksu-nh.defconfig && make O=out ARCH=arm64 -j$(nproc)

sources.name: kernel-zenith
sources.note: This project's desktop kernel, 6.12, x86_64. Never cross with the mobile tree.

sources.name: AOSP x86_64
sources.note: Upstream AOSP built for the aosp_x86_64 lunch target. This is the reference x86_64 Android tree, and it is the one the desktop edition's Android half descends from. No vendor HALs, but the x86_64 target boots in QEMU and on real UEFI hardware.
sources.build_hint: repo init -u https://android.googlesource.com/platform/manifest -b android-15.0.0_r1 && repo sync -c -j8 && lunch aosp_x86_64-trunk_staging-userdebug && m

sources.name: Android-x86
sources.note: Manifest for the Android-x86 project, the tree DarkMatter Exo 4.7 is built from. IMPORTANT: android-x86.org still tells you to init from git.osdn.net, but OSDN is offline -- that host no longer resolves, so those instructions cannot work. This GitHub manifest is AOSP-only (fetch points at .., one remote) and is usable as an AOSP x86_64 base, not as a full Android-x86 tree.
sources.build_hint: repo init -u https://github.com/android-x86/manifest -b master && repo sync -c -j8   # OSDN is dead; see note

sources.name: BlissRoms x86
sources.note: Maintained x86_64 Android fork, the most active of the x86 ROMs still building. Good source for a modern Android half. Branches are codenamed: arcadia-x86 is the current one.

sources.name: AXP.OS
sources.note: Android-x86 derivative still publishing builds, based on Android 13 (axp-a13). Closest living descendant of the Android-x86 lineage that DarkMatter came from.
sources.build_hint: repo init -u https://github.com/AXP-OS/manifest -b axp-a13 && repo sync -c -j8 && lunch aosp_x86_64-userdebug && m

sources.name: LineageOS TV x86_64
sources.note: Device tree (not a manifest) for generic x86_64 TV builds on LineageOS 21. Useful as a working x86_64 device tree to pair with a LineageOS manifest when you want lineage's tooling on x86_64.
sources.build_hint: clone into device/generic/x86_64_tv against a lineage-21.0 manifest

sources.name: DarkMatter Exo 4.7 (prebuilt)
sources.note: Prebuilt ISO, not a source tree: 1,268,467,712 bytes, DarkMatter_Exo4.7.iso. This is the deskop edition's base Android half. Listed because the builder's desktop path consumes it directly, and because its MBR is all zeroes (no partition table), which is why the ISO has to be rebuilt with xorriso rather than patched.
sources.build_hint: download the ISO; fuse_darkmatter_nh.sh extracts it and rebuilds a hybrid image

addons.name: GNOME Shell
addons.note: GNOME session. On Debian/Ubuntu usually installed as the gnome metapackage rather than built.

addons.name: Plasma Mobile
addons.note: Phone-shaped Plasma session, the mobile counterpart to plasma-desktop.

addons.name: Xfce
addons.note: Lightweight session, the usual choice for low-RAM laptops such as the Vivobook Go.

addons.name: Cinnamon
addons.note: Mint's session, also packaged in Debian and Fedora.

addons.name: Budgie
addons.note: GNOME-adjacent session with its own panel.

addons.name: COSMIC
addons.note: Pop!_OS's Rust desktop. Wayland-only, so no X11 session.

addons.name: Sway
addons.note: i3-compatible Wayland tiling compositor. Smallest useful desktop for a fused image.

addons.name: Hyprland
addons.note: Dynamic tiling Wayland compositor. Not in Debian stable, so it needs a newer base.
addons.install: see upstream packaging for your distro

addons.name: Glacier UI
addons.note: A framework-agnostic UI kit, not a compositor and not a shell. Its value here is packages/spec: it emits spec.json plus a JSON Schema describing components, variants, tokens and geometry, so a native renderer can consume the design without running JavaScript. That makes it the bridge from a TypeScript design system to the fused compositor rather than another display server.
addons.build_hint: pnpm install && pnpm --filter @glacier/spec build  # -> packages/spec/dist/spec.json + schema.json

addons.name: Phosh
addons.note: The mobile Wayland shell used as NH-Pro's session. It is a SHELL, not a compositor: the compositor is phoc, which is a separate wlroots-based server. Phosh talks to phoc over wlr-layer-shell plus three private protocols (phosh-private.xml, phoc-device-state-unstable-v1, phoc-layer-shell-effects-unstable-v1). Any compositor that means to host Phosh has to serve those, which is why it cannot be dropped in front of an arbitrary display server.

addons.name: Lipstick
addons.note: Nemo Mobile/Sailfish's homescreen framework, and unlike Phosh it IS a compositor: it subclasses QWaylandCompositor and serves xdg-shell outright. It is Qt/QML, which makes it the natural host for a QML theme generated from Glacier tokens. Two caveats recorded so they are not rediscovered: the tree is Qt6-only (CMakeLists requires 6.2, the rpm spec is still lipstick-qt5 0.36.29), and it carries an alien_bridge_server notification path -- Sailfish's 'Android in a bridge' model, which is the thing AnyRealm replaces with one userspace.

addons.name: ABK CVE Fix
addons.blurb: Patches known CVEs in the kernel source before it compiles.
addons.why: A source-level fix set, so it applies at the kernel stage and must come before the build, not after it.

addons.name: ABK External Module
addons.blurb: Out-of-tree module scaffold used by the other ABK module repos.
addons.why: Needs the built kernel's Module.symvers; a module cannot be linked before the kernel exists.

addons.name: ABK F2FS Fix
addons.blurb: Fixes F2FS behaviour on vendor kernels where the driver is old.
addons.why: Relevant to NURFS because the fused root may sit on F2FS; it is a kernel driver change.

addons.name: ABK Scheduler / Power
addons.blurb: Scheduler and power tweaks aimed at phone thermals and battery.
addons.why: Core scheduler changes, so kernel stage only. Not safe to take as a userspace module.

addons.name: ABK Control Module
addons.blurb: Runtime control surface for the ABK module family.
addons.why: Loads against the running kernel's symbols, so it must be built with the same kernel it will run on.

addons.name: ABK High-Level Hook
addons.blurb: Higher-level hook helpers layered on KernelSU.
addons.why: Depends on KSU being present, which is why the root manager is chosen before this.

addons.name: Brutal Busybox
addons.blurb: Statically linked busybox with a wide applet set.
addons.why: A userspace binary, so it belongs in the system stage and has no kernel constraint.

addons.name: DroidSpaces OSS
addons.blurb: Namespace and mount-isolation helper for Android.
addons.why: Reads carefully: this is the kind of piece AnyRealm replaces with real fusion. Included so it is visible and refusable rather than absent, and it is flagged in the catalog as not used by a NUKI build.

addons.name: KPatch-Next Module
addons.blurb: Live kernel patching control module (branch kpm_ctl0).
addons.why: The branch is not main: pinning it here records that, so a workflow does not silently take main.

addons.name: Kali NetHunter Busybox
addons.blurb: NetHunter's busybox build with the applets its scripts expect.
addons.why: Userspace, system stage. Distinct from Brutal busybox: different applet set and different version.

addons.name: LXC + KernelSU Action
addons.blurb: LXC support wired through KernelSU.
addons.why: Included for completeness and flagged: LXC is a container runtime, which the one-userspace invariant refuses in an image. Selectable only for non-NUKI editions.

addons.name: Module Template (Lua)
addons.blurb: Module template driven from Lua, for scripting an addon.
addons.why: A template, not a fix. Useful as the shape of a new addon rather than as something to install.

addons.name: NetHunter KSU Module
addons.blurb: NetHunter's KernelSU-side module set.
addons.why: Kernel-adjacent and KSU-dependent, so it follows the root-manager choice.

addons.name: ABK CG Module (AOSP 6.1)
addons.blurb: Cgroup module targeting the 6.1 kernel line.
addons.why: Carries its target kernel in its name: 6.1. The mobile target here is 5.10, so it is recorded with that constraint rather than offered blindly.

addons.name: KPatch
addons.blurb: Kernel live-patching support.
addons.why: Kernel stage only; useless as a userspace addon.

addons.name: Motorola Kernel Modules
addons.blurb: Motorola's own kernel modules. Branch is android-10-release.
addons.why: Version-matched to the vendor tree: the 5.10 genevn build cannot use android-10 modules. Kept as a source for reference and for older devices, with the branch stated.

addons.name: NetHunter Static Binaries
addons.blurb: Static binaries NetHunter's tooling expects to find on PATH.
addons.why: Userspace, system stage; static so they do not care which libc the fused root uses.

addons.name: SearchSploit Module
addons.blurb: SearchSploit offline exploit database as a module.
addons.why: Pure userspace data plus a script. System stage, no kernel constraint.

addons.name: rs-module
addons.blurb: Rust-based module.
addons.why: Rust compiles to the system stage normally, but a kernel-side Rust module would need kernel-stage tooling; recorded as system stage until its tree says otherwise.

addons.name: NetHunter Pro Ports
addons.blurb: Port set for Kali NetHunter Pro device bring-up.
addons.why: The desktop edition already merges NH Pro as its user space; this is the per-device port half.

addons.name: GKI KernelSU + SUSFS
addons.blurb: GKI-shaped KernelSU plus SUSFS patch set.
addons.why: Overlaps the chosen root manager's own patch series. Selecting both would apply two SUSFS series to one tree, so the builder refuses that combination rather than producing conflicting hunks.

addons.name: MKSU + SUSFS
addons.blurb: MKSU variant with SUSFS.
addons.why: Same overlap rule as gki-kernelsu-susfs: one root manager and one SUSFS series per tree.

addons.name: Shizuku-Next
addons.blurb: Shizuku fork with several start methods; ships a signed APK per release.
addons.why: An app the user launches, so it is staged into /system/priv-app like the other APKs, not linked into the kernel.
addons.notes: Requires an adb-started or root-started server; both are start methods this fork provides. The APK needs no Zygisk.

addons.name: Sui
addons.blurb: Magisk module giving a modern superuser interface; the APK is embedded in the module.
addons.why: The privileged payload is a module, not a kernel symbol, so it is staged at system time. It must not be compiled into the kernel: Sui hooks Zygote at runtime and needs Zygisk present.
addons.install: the zygisk zip from https://github.com/RikkaApps/Sui/releases carries lib/x86_64/{libmain,librish,libsui}.so plus sepolicy.rule
addons.notes: Requires Zygisk (Magisk 24.0+). Every root manager this builder offers is KernelSU-family and provides no Zygisk, so a composition naming sui is refused. Use shizuku-next instead for privileged-API apps on this kernel.

addons.name: InstallWithOptions
addons.blurb: Installs APKs on-device with advanced options: downgrade, grant-all, install-as-user, and more.
addons.why: A Java/Kotlin app that drives the installer service through Shizuku, so it is staged into /system/priv-app and needs no kernel side at all.
addons.notes: Requires Shizuku running; it does not work standalone. Pair with the shizuku-next addon in the same composition.

addons.name: Minimal Kernel Manager (MKM)
addons.blurb: Floating real-time performance overlay plus kernel management: governor, frequency and parameter tuning, with custom layout and accents.
addons.why: Pure Kotlin over the Shizuku/root API surface, so it is staged into /system/priv-app like the other apps and touches no kernel code.
addons.install: release APK: https://github.com/zenithblue-oss/mkm/releases -> app-release.apk (v1.10, 6 MB, ships all four ABIs)
addons.notes: Works with root OR Shizuku, so it is deliberately not marked as requiring a peer addon: every build here carries KernelSU-Next, which satisfies the root path. Pair it with shizuku-next only if you want the non-root path too. On F-Droid as com.ivarna.mkm; this repo is a mirror of abhay-byte/mkm.

addons.name: DroidVM
addons.blurb: Android virtual machine manager: runs a guest OS with crosvm or QEMU over Qualcomm Gunyah, MediaTek GenieZone or Linux KVM, with its own terminal console and external-display casting.
addons.why: Wanted as an app the user launches, not as a way to build AnyRealm. Staged into /system/priv-app like the other apps; the no-VM rule governs how the OS is composed, not which apps may be installed on it.
addons.notes: arm64 only: it drives an ARM virtualization node, so there is no x86_64 build to stage on the desktop ISO. It also needs a hypervisor node at runtime -- /dev/gunyah, /dev/gzvm or /dev/kvm. Genevn (sm6450) provides Gunyah, so the root path exists there; the desktop kernel has '# CONFIG_KVM is not set', so on dark-hunter the app installs and launches but cannot start a guest until KVM host support is enabled in kernel-zenith. Recorded as an app, not as a build backend.

ux_integrations.name: Ubuntu Touch (tracker)
ux_integrations.note: Not a UX integration and not buildable. The tree is documentation only: README, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, CORE_APPS, SUPPORT, templates, FUNDING. Zero source files of any language. Upstream's own README says it is where bugs and feature requests are tracked for Ubuntu Touch. Including it in a build would contribute eight markdown files.
ux_integrations.what_to_use_instead: The Ubuntu Touch UI is Lomiri (formerly Unity8), which lives in ubports/lomiri and is a Wayland compositor written in C++/QML. That is the tree a UX integration would need, and it is not in this fork.

ux_integrations.name: UBports Installer
ux_integrations.note: A desktop flashing application. It is not a UI for the phone; it is the tool a computer runs to put an OS on the phone. Svelte UI over an Electron shell, speaking adb/fastboot/heimdall to the device.
ux_integrations.why_it_matters_here: Its plugin contract is the useful part and it is the same shape AnyRealm's builder needs. Each OS flavour is a plugin subclassing src/core/plugins/plugin.js with three lifecycle methods: init() -> Promise<boolean>, kill() -> Promise, wait() -> CancelablePromise<string>. Registered by flavour key in plugins/index.js: adb, fastboot, heimdall, systemimage, asteroid_os, lineage_os, postmarketos, core. A mobile_kernel edition is one more plugin, not a fork of the app.

methods.init: Promise<boolean> -- false means do not retry; throw to show the error
methods.wait: CancelablePromise<string> -- block until a device appears

plugin_contract.note: plugins/index.js dispatches per action and logs 'running <plugin> action <fn>', so a new edition adds a flavour key rather than branching inside the app.

ux_integrations.name: postmarketOS aports (pmaports)
ux_integrations.note: Not a UX integration: it is the package repository that lets you choose one. The UI is a package, not a patch: postmarketos-ui-{asteroid,bananui,console,fbkeyboard,framebufferphone,gnome,gnome-mobile,i3wm,kodi,lxqt,mate,phosh,plasma-bigscreen,plasma-desktop,plasma-mobile,shelli,sway,sxmo-de-dwm,sxmo-de-sway,weston}. 114 packages in main/. This is the correct model for AnyRealm's 'compose your own desktop' promise and the reason the UX choice belongs in the builder rather than in the ISO script.
ux_integrations.branch_note: The checked-out branch is danila/courbet ('xiaomi-courbet: new device'), a single-device branch, not postmarketOS master. Building from it would produce a Xiaomi Courbet tree, not a general one.
